anchor_definition: The anchor is the $.get('/User/Passport/token') success callback: it reads the server nonce/ts, computes pwd = Sha1.hash(rawPassword) then pwd = Sha1.hash(nonce+ts+pwd), and posts it as the password field. PLAN section 4.3: the value-construction lives inside this anonymous callback, so it is the smallest complete enclosing function. PLAN section 5.1: not the generic Sha1.hash primitive it calls, and not the outer submit handler that also performs validation.

primary_anchor.why: Anonymous token success callback. Salts the SHA-1 of the password with the freshly fetched nonce+ts (double SHA-1) and posts it to /User/Passport/login. This constructs the exact password value sent in the login request.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: Anonymous token success callback. Salts the SHA-1 of the password with the freshly fetched nonce+ts (double SHA-1) and posts it to /User/Passport/login. This constructs the exact password value sent in the login request.

The login submit click handler validates the fields, fetches the token, and contains the anchor callback. It is target-specific and would reach the right behavior, but it is coarser than the smallest function that actually derives the final password value.
Reusable SHA-1 implementation used twice by the anchor. It computes the hash primitive but does not combine nonce+ts or bind the result to the login password field.
Generic SHA-1 rotate-left helper used inside Sha1.hash. It is below the hashing primitive and has no login-specific semantics.
Generic SHA-1 word-to-hex formatter used to produce the final hash string. It formats hash words but does not build the salted password.
Generic UTF-8 encoder called by Sha1.hash before hashing. It supports the primitive but is not target-specific.
Generic jQuery shorthand wrapper used for both token fetch and login post. It forwards options to ajax but does not derive the password value.
The /User/Passport/login response callback runs after the password field has already been constructed and sent. It is on the same request path but is response handling, not value construction.
Pressing Enter focuses and clicks the login button, entering the same submit path. It is a trigger helper upstream of the nonce/hash logic.
Generic network sink reached after the anchor has placed the derived password into the post data. It emits an already constructed request.
A page search-bar helper (navigates to the search results page); unrelated to the login password path.
Validates the search-box keyword; unrelated to the login password path.
Header login-status initializer that fetches login_bar/logout UI state. It contains Passport-looking URLs but is not the password hashing login flow.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The exact anchor is the token success callback that has both the server nonce/ts and the raw password available and constructs the final `password` field.
The outer submit click handler is target-specific but too broad: it includes validation and callback setup in addition to the anchor.
Sha1.hash and its helpers are generic primitives and should stay at 0.5 even though the hash bytes determine the final value.
jQuery get/post/ajax wrappers send or schedule already prepared data and should not outrank the callback that constructs `pwd`.
Response callbacks, header login-bar code and page-search helpers are not constructors for the requested password field.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.
audit_notes: Answer match check: 1.json case 17 code begins at the same $.get token request and anonymous success callback represented by oracle.primary_anchor.
Question direction check: the visible question asks for the function whose own body combines fetched nonce/ts with the hashed password and posts it, so it points to the anonymous token callback.

Span maps to the reusable SHA-1/UTF-8 primitive used by the anchor.
